args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. The SRE agent rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback check: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate about 0.2%. Note: the v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging before it was promoted to production. v2.3.1 needs root-cause analysis before anyone deploys it again.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back from v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **Why v2.3.0:** It's the most recent release that was healthy in production. The only newer build, v2.3.1-rc, ran in staging rather than production, and it was unhealthy there too.
- **Rollback:** us-east, us-west and eu-west are all now on v2.3.0. The service passes health checks, and the error rate dropped from about 18% to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It explains the failure, the rollback and the current health. It also notes that v2.3.1 was already failing in staging before it went to production, so it needs a root-cause analysis before anyone tries to deploy it again.

content.text: I'll start by checking the current status and the deployment history.
The most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0. v2.3.1-rc was a staging build and was unhealthy, so it doesn't count. Rolling back now.
The service is healthy again and there's no existing incident, so I'll open one.
